source.title: Proxy-Tuning: Tailoring Multimodal Autoregressive Models for Subject-Driven Image Generation
source.authors: Yi Wu; Sheng-Ju Qian; Lingting Zhu; Lei Liu; Wandi Qiao; Ziqiang Li; Le-Quan Yu; Bin Li

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests weak-supervision fine-tuning in subject-driven image generation, a vision setting, using diffusion supervisors and autoregressive students.
record.gate_note: The paper does not calculate Burns et al.'s PGR. It compares CLIP-I, CLIP-T and DINO scores, and reports a user study. Direct DreamBooth fine-tuning and data augmentation results are not rows because they do not test fine-tuning on weaker-model-generated proxy data. Reported values for the proxy-tuned AR models and their supervisors are recorded separately by model, supervisor and metric.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes pretrained AR image generators (LlamaGen 0.775B, Lumina-mGPT 7B) on images from DreamBooth-tuned diffusion supervisors (SDXL, SD3, SD3.5, FLUX). It compares student and supervisor on CLIP-I, DINO, CLIP-T and human ratings. This is a new, vision setting for V1/V6 and also bears on V3 through student architecture and supervisor choice. Two caveats: no PGR or true-label ceiling is reported, and the 'weak' supervisors are 2B–12B, larger than LlamaGen, so 'weak' is the authors' framing rather than a size relation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim AR students 'consistently' beat their diffusion supervisors in both subject fidelity and prompt adherence, and that the effect is specific to AR students. They rest the prompt-adherence claim on the 9-person user study and treat CLIP-T, which mostly shows a drop, as a flawed metric. The paraphrase should note that 'consistently' is not borne out for LlamaGen with FLUX.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a weaker model to generate proxy training examples and fine-tunes a stronger pretrained student, but the setting is image generation, the supervision consists of generated images rather than task labels, and the evaluation does not calculate PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by supervisor and student model; CLIP-T does not track the subject-fidelity gains consistently, and the user study reports higher prompt-fidelity ratings than CLIP-T suggests.
record.problems: The paper does not report PGR or a true-label strong-model ceiling. Most automated measurements are similarity metrics; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The user study has 9 participants. Table 4 and Table 5 are flattened in the supplied text, limiting reliable assignment of some values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4's per-model numeric values are not entered because the flattened presentation does not permit confident pairing of each value with a model and supervisor; its explicit aggregate conclusion is recorded in R25. Table 5's numerical cells are likewise not assigned individually; its stated aggregate multi-subject finding is recorded in R29.

untested.parts: No PGR and no strong ceiling trained on true labels. Direct DreamBooth tuning of the AR models scores below the supervisor (Table 1), so a PGR denominator would not be meaningful here.
Not tested: no auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling or loss variants.
No NLP, chess or reward-modelling tasks; no representation-based predictors; no systematic size sweep of student or supervisor.
Not tested: no exploitation, distribution-shift or shared-error analysis.
Not tested: no theory; the authors list theory as future work.
Only subject-driven image generation; no classification or other vision tasks.

missing.what: Per-model diffusion-student values. CLIP-T is slightly up for SD3 (+0.01%) and SD3.5 (+0.42%), while CLIP-I and DINO are down for all four.
Per-supervisor values for the joint multi-subject AR student vs separate supervisors
User-study scores for the fine-tuned diffusion supervisor (4.185/3.963/4.370) as the proper baseline for R26-R28

record.verdict_notes: The 'weak' supervisors (2B–12B) are larger than LlamaGen (0.775B). The AR students tuned directly on the same reference images score well below the supervisors (Table 1). So 'strong' here means a pretrained AR architecture, not a more capable model on the task. No uncertainty is reported for any metric, and differences such as R20, R22 and R24 are small.

versions.untested_parts: No PGR is calculated, and the paper does not measure a strong model trained on true labels as a ceiling.
Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, and loss variants are not tested.
The study varies model architectures and sizes in image generation, but does not test NLP, chess, reward modelling, or representation-based predictors of PGR.
No weak-supervisor-checkability exploit, distribution-shift test, or analysis of shared student-supervisor errors is reported.
No theoretical conditions for students beating supervisors are tested or derived.
Tests vision image generation only; no other non-language modality is tested.

rows.note: The paper says this weak-to-strong phenomenon did not occur for diffusion students. Table 4's flattened values are not assigned to individual models here.
rows.check: Diffusion-to-diffusion proxy tuning is not clearly a weak-to-strong pairing, so it bears on V3 (student architecture) and V6, not V1. rows.subject: LlamaGen (joint multi-subject Proxy-Tuning)
rows.operation_detail: One AR student was trained jointly on proxy data from separate subject-specific diffusion supervisors.
rows.measure: Subject fidelity (authors' summary of quantitative results)
rows.baseline: Individual diffusion supervisors, each specialized for one subject
rows.value: Authors state the joint AR model matches the subject fidelity of the individual supervisors.
rows.note: The paper also reports that the joint AR model exceeds the separate-supervisor values in the displayed CLIP-I and DINO series, but the flattened table does not reliably pair each value with a supervisor.
rows.check: Table 5 is readable. Joint LlamaGen students score CLIP-I 0.7713/0.7773/0.7597 and DINO 0.7176/0.7335/0.7235. The separate supervisors (SDXL/SD3/SD3.5) score CLIP-I 0.7616/0.7501/0.7567 and DINO 0.7040/0.6965/0.7028. Each student exceeds its supervisor, so the state is observed, not partial.

relationships.condition: Subject fidelity (CLIP-I, DINO) for Lumina-mGPT with all four supervisors and LlamaGen with SDXL/SD3/SD3.5; human subject-fidelity ratings; joint multi-subject LlamaGen
relationships.reason: Students exceed supervisors on CLIP-I and DINO (R1, R3, R4, R6, R7, R9, R10, R12, R13, R15, R16, R18, R19, R21). Human subject-fidelity rating is 4.593 vs 3.963 (R27). The joint student beats each supervisor (R29).
relationships.display_finding: Students exceeded supervisors on CLIP-I and DINO, achieved human subject-fidelity ratings of 4.593 versus 3.963, and outperformed each supervisor in joint multi-subject generation.

source_check.reason: Tables 2–3 show higher subject-fidelity scores in the specified pairs; Table 6 gives 4.593 versus supervisor 3.963; Table 5 shows corresponding joint students above their separate supervisors.

relationships.reason: CLIP-T is below the supervisor in 7 of 8 pairs (R2, R5, R8, R11, R14, R17, R23) and only negligibly above for Lumina/FLUX (R20). Human ratings show only small gains (R26, R28). The result depends on whether prompt fidelity is measured by metric or by raters.
relationships.display_finding: CLIP-T fell below the supervisor in 7 of 8 pairs and improved negligibly for Lumina/FLUX, while human ratings showed small gains.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Prompt results depend on evaluation: CLIP-T falls in seven pairs and rises slightly in one, while human prompt fidelity and image quality improve. This mixed condition group qualifies the broader effect.

relationships.reason: The student is below the supervisor on all three metrics (R22-R24), contradicting the authors' 'consistently outperform' claim for this pair.
relationships.display_finding: The student scored below its supervisor on all three metrics.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.reason: Table 3 places LlamaGen below FLUX on CLIP-I, CLIP-T and DINO, reversing the claimed supervisor advantage for this pair.

relationships.condition: Dependence on student architecture and supervisor
relationships.reason: Gains appear for AR students but not for diffusion students (R25). The smaller LlamaGen loses its subject-fidelity gain under the strongest supervisor, FLUX (R22, R24), while Lumina keeps it (R19, R21).
relationships.display_finding: Gains appeared for autoregressive students but not diffusion students, and FLUX supervision removed subject-fidelity gains for smaller LlamaGen while Lumina retained them.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Dependence on student architecture and supervisor
source_check.reason: Lumina-mGPT retains subject-fidelity gains with FLUX while LlamaGen loses them; Table 4 also shows architecture-dependent outcomes. This supports pairing dependence without measuring PGR or independently establishing a capability hierarchy.

relationships.display_finding: CLIP-I and DINO scores exceeded supervisors in most pairs, consistent with human subject-fidelity ratings.

tranche.reason: Tests supervisor-to-student generalization in a new setting: subject-driven image generation using diffusion-generated proxy images to fine-tune autoregressive students.

source_check.notes: No PGR, true-label strong ceiling, or independent capability-gap check is reported. Table 5 is readable despite R29's note; R20's small positive difference supports partial, but the paper does not establish negligibility.

statements.correction: Tables 2–3: CLIP-I and DINO exceed the supervisor in seven of eight pairs; LlamaGen/FLUX is below on both. CLIP-T is below in seven of eight pairs. Table 6: Lumina-mGPT/SDXL human prompt fidelity 4.481 versus 4.370.
statements.problem: The subject-fidelity clause omits the LlamaGen/FLUX exception.

statements.correction: Tables 2–3: CLIP-T falls in seven of eight pairs; Lumina-mGPT/FLUX 0.3155 versus 0.3144. Table 6: human prompt fidelity for proxy-tuned Lumina-mGPT 4.481 versus fine-tuned SDXL 4.370. Table 4: diffusion students have lower CLIP-I and DINO than their DreamBooth baselines.
statements.problem: The opening claim about prompt fidelity is broader than the evidence: human prompt ratings improve, and Lumina-mGPT/FLUX has a small positive CLIP-T difference. The paper does not establish that this difference is negligible.
